idea.selected_primary_direction: D2 — Stereochemical Closure, Not a Preferred Hand: A Tiered Test of Chirality's Functional Necessity for Chemical Life
idea.rejected_direction: D4 — All life must use terrestrial handedness

core_conclusion: Biological homochirality is a strong functional constraint in known terrestrial molecular architectures.
Stereochemical closure—repeatable compatibility among monomers, templates, catalysts, and recognition partners—is a more defensible research target than a universally preferred hand.
Neither universal homochirality nor the impossibility of alternative cross-chiral or achiral life architectures is established.
human_review_required: Check the survey's interpretation against the cited primary literature.
Have stereochemistry, RNA, and origins-of-life specialists assess the codebook and architecture classifications.
Review the philosophical and scientific scope of the adopted life-definition contracts.
Route any future empirical work through independent safety, ethics, and institutional compliance review.
known_limitations: No new experiment, simulation, synthesis, or biological observation was performed.
The historical mechanism that established terrestrial homochirality remains unresolved.
The work does not establish a mirror organism or an achiral life form.
Definitions of life and heterogeneity in the cited literature can change the scope of the conclusion.
